reference_benchmarks.name: CMI-Bench
reference_benchmarks.coverage: 14 traditional MIR task families across 20 datasets reformulated as open-ended music instruction following
reference_benchmarks.finding: The authors report significant gaps between evaluated audio-text LLMs and task-specific supervised MIR systems under standard MIR metrics, together with cultural, chronological, and gender biases.
reference_benchmarks.product_implication: Fluent audio-language output is not evidence of exact MIR competence; specialized engines remain authoritative unless matched-task evaluation proves otherwise.

reference_benchmarks.name: MUSE
reference_benchmarks.coverage: 10 fundamental music perception and auditory relational reasoning tasks with a 200-person human baseline
reference_benchmarks.finding: The benchmark reports a persistent human gap; Qwen2.5-Omni and Audio Flamingo 3 perform at or near chance on several tasks, and chain-of-thought prompting is inconsistent and often detrimental.
reference_benchmarks.product_implication: Do not assume a general audio-language model can supply reliable relational music facts; evaluate semantic explanation as a separate capability.

notes: This artifact records upstream reference evidence only. No hello-ai audio-language checkpoint was loaded or run in this stage.
